title: Drill: Euclid's GCD
prompt: From memory: return the greatest common divisor of `a` and `b` (both ≥ 0, not both 0) using Euclid's algorithm — recursive or iterative.

solution.explanation: gcd(a, b) = gcd(b, a mod b) because any common divisor of a and b also divides the remainder. It stops when b reaches 0. The remainder at least halves every two steps, so O(log min(a, b)) time and O(log) recursion depth.

hints: Any common divisor of a and b also divides a % b. Can you shrink the problem?
gcd(a, b) = gcd(b, a % b). The numbers shrink until one of them is 0.
Base case: `b == 0` means the answer is `a`. One line: `return b == 0 ? a : gcd(b, a % b);`

title: Transpose bounds
prompt: In the transpose loop, why does `j` start at `i + 1` instead of 0?
options: Starting at 0 would swap every pair twice, undoing the transpose entirely
To skip the diagonal for speed
explanation: Each (i,j)/(j,i) pair must swap exactly once — iterating only the upper triangle guarantees that. j from 0 visits both (1,2) and (2,1), swapping back to the original.

title: Drill: reverse the digits
prompt: From memory (digit peel/build): return the digits of `x` reversed (x >= 0, result fits in int). Peel with `% 10` / `/= 10`, build with `r = r * 10 + digit`.

solution.explanation: Peeling from the right and appending on the right reverses the digit order. Trailing zeros disappear on their own (100 → 1). O(number of digits) time, O(1) space.

hints: How do you get the last digit of a number, and how do you remove it?
`x % 10` is the last digit and `x /= 10` drops it. Loop until x is 0.
Append each digit to the result: `r = r * 10 + x % 10`.

title: Zeroes: why row 0 last?
prompt: In the O(1)-space Set Matrix Zeroes, row 0 stores the column markers (`m[0][c] == 0` means zero column c). Why must row 0 itself be zeroed at the very end?
options: Zeroing it earlier would overwrite the column markers, and every column would look marked
Java requires the first row to be processed last
It doesn't matter when row 0 is zeroed
explanation: The markers ARE row 0 (and column 0). Zeroing row 0 before the interior pass makes `m[0][c] == 0` true for every c, which wipes the whole matrix. Apply the interior first, then column 0 (using `m[0][0]`), then row 0 (using the separate `row0` flag).

title: Recall: fast exponentiation
prompt: Fill in the O(log n) Pow(x, n) template, including the overflow-safe negative exponent.
explanation: Widen to `long` so `-Integer.MIN_VALUE` fits. Each iteration looks at the lowest bit of N. If it is set, multiply the current power into the result. Then square the base (x, x², x⁴, …) and halve N. That is O(log n) multiplications.
